findings.summary: Soundness: briefs come from a new file format that nothing writes, while the real waiting Steward proposals are left unread. On the real repository the decisions page will always say 'Nothing is waiting'.
findings.evidence: build_decisions reads `records/decisions-waiting/*.json`. The design note says a later change will write these files, and no component writes them today. A Steward proposal above its limit is already recorded: steward::decide returns Decision::Proposed and keeps the WorkItem, which is an `athena.work-item/1` record (athena-data records.rs:1853) with kind `Proposal`. xtask already depends on athena-data (xtask/Cargo.toml), so the design note's reason (xtask does not depend on athena-core) does not apply. `Brief::from_proposal` and `WaitingProposal` are marked dead outside tests. The request says to render a brief 'for each item that waits for a person', and steward.rs was on the deliverables list but is unchanged. Simpler and more correct: build briefs from WorkItem records with kind Proposal, read through athena-data.

findings.summary: Soundness: the record links are relative paths that will not open on the published site, so the 'every claim links to its record' rule is not met in practice.
findings.evidence: record_link writes href="records/..." into decisions/<id>.html. A browser resolves that to <site>/decisions/records/..., and records/ is not published with the site. The existing explainer already builds working links with source_url(base, sha, path, ...), using the base and commit from the study pin. The brief renderer should do the same. The test only checks that the href string is present, not that it resolves.

findings.summary: Soundness: the Steward-proposal brief is fixed text. Every proposal gets the recommendation 'Approve' and the same cost, risk and reason, each linked to a record that does not say it.
findings.evidence: from_proposal hard-codes the cost 'One queued job changes the rung.', the risk 'The change touches a rung above Steward's limit.', the risk levels 2 and 1, and the recommendation 'Approve' with the reason 'The evidence supports the finding.'. None of this is read from the proposal or its evidence, yet each line is shown with a 'record:' link as if it came from that record. This shows the owner a recommendation and sources that Athena never worked out. If the content is not derived from records, it should be marked as a template, or the field should be refused.

findings.summary: The word count leaves out the brief title, though the owner reads it as prose.
findings.evidence: prose() includes the decision, option fields and recommendation but not `title`, which appears as the page's h1. A long title can push a page past the 120-word limit and still pass check().

findings.summary: Source links accept any URL scheme.
findings.evidence: record_link escapes the source but does not restrict the scheme, so a javascript: URL would be rendered as a working link. Today the input is trusted records, so the risk is low.

summary: The candidate stores the owner's style rules verbatim and adds a brief renderer to the existing xtask site renderer. The renderer refuses a brief with no recommendation or more than 120 words, and the site now has a decisions page linked from the index. The changelog entry and design note are in place, and all six acceptance criteria pass by the targeted tests I ran and the recorded CI run. It still fails on soundness, for three reasons. First, briefs are read from a new `records/decisions-waiting/*.json` format that nothing writes, while the real waiting Steward proposals sit unread. They are WorkItem records of kind Proposal, readable through athena-data, which xtask already depends on. So on the real repository the decisions page would always say nothing is waiting. Second, the record links are relative `records/...` paths that won't open from the published decisions pages. The explainer already builds working links to the source repository with `source_url`. Third, `from_proposal` gives every proposal the same fixed cost, risk and 'Approve' recommendation, each shown with a record link as if it came from that record. My site build ran on the snapshot, which has no records/, so its '0 briefs' result does not describe the real repository.
